executive_summary.question: What two types of conduct constitute the offence of 'stalking' under BNS section 78?
executive_summary.generated_answer:
The offence of **stalking** under **BNS section 78(1)** is constituted by either of the following two types of conduct:

1. **Following a woman and contacting (or attempting to contact) her to foster personal interaction repeatedly**, despite a clear indication of disinterest from her.  
2. **Monitoring the use by a woman of the internet, e‑mail, or any other form of electronic communication**.  

These are the two distinct behaviours listed in sub‑section (1) of section 78 that together define the offence of stalking.

evidence_analysis.claim_text: The first type of conduct is following a woman and contacting (or attempting to contact) her to foster personal interaction repeatedly, despite a clear indication of disinterest from her.
evidence_analysis.supporting_evidence:
(1) Any man who—
(i) follows a woman and contacts, or attempts to contact such woman to foster
personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest by such woman; or
(ii) monitors the use by a woman of the internet, e-mail or any other form of
electronic communication,
commits the offence of stalking:
Provided that such conduct shall not amount to stalking if the man who pursued it
proves that—
(i) it was pursued for the purpose of preventing or detecting crime and the man
accused of stalking had been entrusted with the responsibility of prevention and
detection of crime by the State; or
(ii) it was pursued under any law or to comply with any condition or requirement
imposed by any person under any law; or
(iii) in the particular circumstances such conduct was reasonable and justified.
